discipline_framing: natural language processing and sentiment analysis for trend intelligence — processing millions of social media posts, reviews, and search queries to measure the emotional undercurrents of the public
audience: a motivated learner progressing from competent beginner toward expert practitioner in NLP-driven trend and sentiment analysis
sources: Jurafsky & Martin, Speech and Language Processing (3rd ed. draft); Manning & Schütze, Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing
Liu, Sentiment Analysis: Mining Opinions, Sentiments, and Emotions; Pang & Lee, Opinion Mining and Sentiment Analysis (foundations and trends)

canonical papers: Mikolov et al. (word2vec), Pennington et al. (GloVe), Blei et al. (LDA), Devlin et al. (BERT), Vaswani et al. (Attention Is All You Need), Hamilton et al. (diachronic word embeddings)
social-media NLP: Eisenstein, Natural Language Processing for Social Media; Blodgett et al. on dialect bias; Barbieri et al. (emoji and Twitter semantics)
VADER (Hutto & Gilbert) documentation and SemEval shared-task archives (sentiment, ABSA, stance, irony)
annotation and evaluation: Pustejovsky & Stubbs, Natural Language Annotation for Machine Learning; datasheets for datasets (Gebru et al.); benchmark-contamination literature

platform data docs: Google Trends methodology documentation, Wikipedia pageviews API docs, current platform API terms (X, Reddit, TikTok Research API); AoIR ethical guidelines for internet research; Bender & Gebru, On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots
pitfalls: trusting lexicon sentiment scores on out-of-domain text without validation
ignoring sarcasm, irony, slang drift, and dialect variation — and shipping models with dialect bias
confusing message volume and engagement with sentiment or public mood
aggregate mood claims built on unvalidated micro-level scores (ecological fallacy)
scraping and collecting text data in violation of ToS, privacy law, or research ethics
overclaiming emotion-detection accuracy and treating benchmarks as ground truth in the LLM era
